catalog_quote: In general, Nyoro nouns include two underlying tone patterns: they are either penultimate high or ultimate high, regardless of the number of syllables that constitute words (…σσ́σ, …σσσ́). It is also important to note that there are no entirely low-toned words (…σσσ). The tone bearing unit is the syllable, and both short and long vowels and diphthongs behave in the same manner. For the sake of reference, penultimate high-toned nouns are called “tone pattern A nouns,” while ultimate high-toned nouns are referred to as “tone pattern B nouns.” [...] Generally, in tone pattern A nouns, high tones are realized as falling in isolation. However, they are set right when the pause is eliminated, as in (2), where the possessive adjective -ánge (“my”) directly follows the head noun. new_statements.rule_in_words: Every Nyoro word carries exactly one underlying High, located either on the penultimate or on the final syllable (a lexical two-way choice for nouns; no toneless words; all preceding syllables Low). Before pause a penult H surfaces as a fall (…F-L) and a final H is anticipated onto the penult and surfaces as …H-F; phrase-medially the underlying positions show (…H-L vs …H-H). Verb infinitives and most conjugated forms take the penult-H pattern; monosyllabic-root infinitives and certain TAM forms take the final-H pattern. Kaji calls this 'tone' (a two-pattern, '2型' system) while noting it is debatable whether such a language is a tone language; nothing is said about stress as distinct from this H.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; all syllables before the final two are Low.
new_statements.exceptions: Monosyllabic (-CV-) verb infinitives take final H (okúlyâ 'to eat') whereas all other infinitives take penult H (Kaji 2018: 192; Kaji 2021 ILCAA fn.9); verb TAM forms select pattern A or B grammatically and nine affirmative tenses undergo High Tone Deletion (Kaji 2021 KSU 54).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level underlying H; citation (pre-pausal) forms differ from phrase-medial forms: isolation A = …FL, B = …HF; before a following word A = …HL, B = …HH (Kaji 2021 ILCAA ch.7 p.144-145, exx. (1)-(3)). Same facts stated in Japanese in the dedicated chapter: 'ニョロ語の声調言語としての特徴は、いわゆる 2 型の言語であるということである。つまり、単語を構成する音節数に関わりなく、声調のパターンは 2 つしかない。' (p.141) and '基底形では、最後 2 音節が、A 型の単語は HL、そして B 型の単語は LH となる。最後 2 音節より前はすべて L である。' (p.145).
new_statements.identity_note: All Kaji sources describe Nyoro proper (Orunyoro, JE11, fieldwork based in Hoima, Bunyoro) = nyor1246. Not to be conflated with Tooro (toor1238), the other half of the 'Runyoro-Rutooro' written standard, which Kaji describes as having lost the lexical contrast (H always on the penult in isolation). Rubongoya 1999 and Maddox 1902 treat Runyoro-Rutooro jointly.

sources.note: Sec. 2 'Nyoro nominal tone' (p.274-276): two underlying patterns only, H on penult (pattern A) or H on final syllable (pattern B), regardless of word length; no all-L words; TBU = syllable; penult H realized as falling before pause; final H anticipated onto penult and realized HF before pause. No mention of stress.

sources.citation: 梶茂樹 [Kaji, Shigeki]. 2021. ニョロ語の声調 [The tone of Nyoro]. Ch. 7 in 梶茂樹 (ed.) アフリカ諸語の声調・アクセント, 141-162. Tokyo: ILCAA (CC BY 4.0), hdl:10108/99918.
sources.note: Dedicated 22-page description: Nyoro is a '2型' (two-pattern) system - whatever the syllable count, the last two syllables are either FL (underlying...HL, 'A型') or HF (underlying...LH, 'B型'), everything before is L (p.141, 143-145); minimal pairs (p.142-3); author notes it is debatable whether such a language should be called a tone language but uses 'tone' (p.141); verb infinitives all A-type except monosyllabic verbs; summary (39) p.160. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Kaji, Shigeki. 2018. Do we need to postulate a different tone pattern for monosyllabic verbs in Nyoro? Acta Humanistica et Scientifica Universitatis Sangio Kyotiensis, Humanities Series 51: 189-205.
sources.note: p.189-191: Nyoro has two noun tone patterns regardless of length, underlying H on the ultimate syllable (here called A) or on the penultimate (here B); Tooro by contrast has one pattern (penult H). Infinitives take the penult-H pattern except monosyllabic verbs. No stress statement. (Note: A/B labels are swapped relative to Kaji 2021.)
